rules_a_to_k.how: Option on gu_site: 'A region such as the pelvis or groin, with no organ named' sends the clerk to the general carcinoma site screen, because a region names no organ; its reason states that the site follows the tissue the tumour type implies.
Hint on gu_site: a report naming only perivesical, periprostatic or periurethral tissue does not name that organ. The paraurethral gland, which ICD-O lists, is its own answer (C68.1).
Options on gu_site: two parts of the bladder take C67.8; two urinary organs C68.8; two male genital organs C63.8; two parts of the penis C60.8. Each reason names the code.
Referral only: every lymphoma answer refers to Group 2, which applies Rule D.
No leukaemia reaches these screens; lymphoma and leukaemia go to Groups 2 and 1.

Hints on gu_not_malignant_urinary, gu_not_malignant_prostate and gu_not_malignant_penis: a stated invasion (pT1 or higher) sends the clerk back to the carcinoma answer. The inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour option's reason: a report calling it malignant is a sarcoma (8825/3, Group 9). The urothelial picker hint: a papillary urothelial carcinoma is chosen there only when the report states invasion.

No screen offers a grade: low-grade and high-grade non-invasive papillary carcinoma share 8130/2, invasive urothelial grades share 8120/3, and Gleason grade and penile grade do not change the code. The sixth digit is not built.

Picker labels and reasons on gu_prostate_picker: ductal adenocarcinoma (8500/3, breast attached in ICD-O) and basal cell carcinoma (8147/3 basal cell carcinoma of prostate, not 8090/3 skin) keep C61.9; the picker hint says so. The deposit option on every histology screen sends a tumour that began elsewhere to its primary site.
Hint on gu_urinary_picker, gu_prostate_picker and gu_penis_picker: if the term is not found, search its words in a different order.

Hint on every histology screen and picker: when two terms describe one tumour and no answer covers both, choose the higher code. gu_urinary_picker's hint gives the manual's own example, transitional cell epidermoid carcinoma 8120/3. Registrar questions 2 and 3 ask whether WHO subtype codes lower than 8120 or 8085 stand against Rule K.

conflicts.issue: ICCC-2017 places nephroblastoma (VIa1) and these renal cell carcinomas (VIb) in Group 6 at every site, so at the renal pelvis they refer to Group 6. Every carcinoma of the kidney (C64.9) is VIb. A urothelial carcinoma of the renal pelvis that invades the kidney stays C65.9 (pT3).
8310/3 is Clear cell renal cell carcinoma at the kidney (VIb) and Mullerian clear cell adenocarcinoma at the renal pelvis (XIf10); the site answer decides.

Rhabdomyosarcoma (IXa) and malignant rhabdoid tumour (IXd3 at these sites) refer to Group 9. Inflammatory myofibroblastic tumour is 8825/1 in ICD-O-3.2 and is not registrable; only a report calling it malignant (8825/3 Myofibroblastic sarcoma, IXb1) refers to Group 9.
Extragonadal germ cell tumours at these sites are Xb. A urothelial carcinoma with trophoblastic differentiation is 8120/3 (Netto 2022 Table 3), not choriocarcinoma 9100/3. Testis (C62) is Group 10.
Paraganglioma of the bladder, which the WHO urothelial table lists, is ICCC-2017 IVb.

Prostatic stromal sarcoma 8935/3 is XIIa4; mesothelioma of the tunica vaginalis is XIIa5. The tissue-free answer 8000/3 falls in XIIb at every site in this part, so a clinical or imaging registration records a Group 12 case.

ICCC-2017 puts carcinomas of penis, NOS (C60.9) and scrotum (C63.2) in XIe. At C60.9, 8083, 8084, 8085, 8086 and 8120 fall in no ICCC range; at C60.0 to C60.8, basal cell carcinoma 8090/3 falls in no range. Ruling 3 keeps them in Group XI; the subgroup is computed from the site (registrar question 8).
